29.0.s.en: (1) A call to worship the Lord

29.0.0.en: 1- "Give unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, give unto the Lord glory and strength."

29.0.1.en: 1- God rejoices in the offerings of His children, and by His children is meant those who believe in Him, who love Him and present Him their gifts, and before their gifts they present their hearts.

29.0.2.en: 2- The children of God believe in Him, so they glorify Him, because there is no other God but He. As for the gods of the nations, they are demons and have no value.

29.0.3.en: 3- What is meant by giving glory and strength to God is praising His holy name, thanking Him for His power that protects His children, and glorifying Him for all His works with them.

29.1.0.en: 2- "Give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name; worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness."

29.1.1.en: 1- God's name means His person, so glorifying His name means glorifying Him. This glorifying lifts the heart and attaches it to God, so that it rises above every sin.

29.1.2.en: 2- Glorifying God is accomplished not only by the praise of the lips, but also by good works and every act of mercy and help toward others.

29.1.3.en: 3- The believer is called to give to God three times, after the pattern of the Holy Trinity; that is, whoever gives to God receives the blessing of the Holy Trinity.

29.1.4.en: 4- In the Septuagint there is also mention of bringing the young of rams, that is, the sacrifices offered in the tabernacle of the congregation and in the tent of Solomon, as proof of the believers' love for God. Thus the believers are called to bring to God four times: the three mentioned here, with the offering of the young of rams added to them. The believers' bringing offerings to God four times is a type of presenting these gifts in the four corners of the world, that is, the whole world. This is completed when the Gentiles believe in Christ and offer the sacrifices of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord, in every place in the world.

29.1.5.en: 5- After presenting their love to God in offerings, the believers are called to submit to Him with reverence, so he says to them, worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness, that is, in modest clothing, without preoccupation with material things, and with readiness to obey His commandments.

29.1.6.en: 6- In the Septuagint, that is, in the Agpeya, it says, worship the Lord in His holy court; and what is meant by the holy court is the tabernacle of the congregation and the temple of Solomon, then after this the Church in the New Testament, and finally the perfect holy court is the Kingdom of Heaven.

29.1.7.en: God rejoices in all your offerings, so do not be stingy toward God with the offerings of your mouth's praises, and likewise with works of mercy, and thus you gladden His heart with your love and your response to Him.

29.2.0.en: 3- "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters: the God of glory thundereth: the Lord is upon many waters."

29.2.1.en: 1- David felt that the sound coming from the tumult of the waters is the voice of God, the Creator of these waters, whether in the seas or the rivers, declaring His mastery over them; for it is He who controls the seas by the phenomenon of the tides and does not let them cover the dry land.

29.2.2.en: 2- Before the beginning of creation the world was waters and darkness, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters, and it was He who created the heaven and the air, gathered the waters into collections, and caused the dry land to appear. So the Spirit of God is the secret of the life of all creation, and He thunders with His power, declaring that He is the Creator, just as He also thundered on the day of Pentecost, declaring that He created the Church, and He dwells in all who believe in Him, giving them a life that lasts forever.

29.2.3.en: 3- The many waters signify mankind, whether Jews or Gentiles. And the voice of God above them means that He is the Creator of all mankind.

29.2.4.en: 4- The voice of the Lord means the incarnate Hypostasis of the Son, who is the Word of God who appears as a voice that we hear; for "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him" (Jn 1:18).

29.2.5.en: 5- The phrase "the voice of the Lord" is repeated seven times in this psalm, declaring the perfection of Christ, because the number 7 signifies perfection. And He has given us salvation by His Holy Spirit in the seven sacraments of the Church. And we hear the voice of the Lord in His saving work in these sacraments.

29.2.6.en: 6- When the voice of the Lord thunders, it frightens the wicked, because it judges them, but it reassures the children of God, as it declares that He is their support in all tribulations; for the many waters also signify tribulations, but the Lord above them reassures His children that He is the Controller of all, and no harm touches them as long as He is with them.

29.3.0.en: 4- "The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is full of majesty."

29.3.1.en: 1- The voice of the Lord is full of power, so it troubled the wicked, like Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who pursued the children of Israel and entered the Red Sea, and God troubled them through the pillar of fire, until the wheels of their chariots came off (Ex 14:25); and likewise He troubled the Philistines in the days of Samuel (1 Sam 7:10).

29.3.2.en: 2- The voice of the Lord was powerful when it declared of Christ, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased," when He was transfigured on Mount Tabor with Moses and Elijah. And His majesty and greatness appeared clearly before His disciples.

29.3.3.en: 3- Christ spoke as one having authority and not as the scribes, so His speech was with power and also with majesty, even when He appeared in weakness, when the soldiers came to arrest Him and He asked them, "Whom seek ye?" and they said, "Jesus of Nazareth," and then He said to them, "I am he," and they fell to the ground on their faces, for fear of His power and greatness (Jn 18:6).

29.4.0.en: 5- "The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars; yea, the Lord breaketh the cedars of Lebanon."

29.4.1.en: 6- "He maketh them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox."

29.4.2.en: The cedars of Lebanon: a tall, gigantic, evergreen tree, whose wood is strong and is not broken by violent winds; rather, the tree is uprooted, yet the wind cannot break it.

29.4.4.en: Sirion: a name given to Mount Hermon, a mountain lying southeast of Lebanon, very high, reaching a height of about 3000 meters.

29.4.5.en: The young of the wild ox: quick to flee and run away; what is meant is the young of the wild ox, which are swift to run away.

29.4.6.en: 1- If the cedar trees of Lebanon represent strength and greatness, and signify the pride of man, then God by His mighty voice breaks this cedar and subjects man's pride to Himself.

29.4.7.en: 2- The wicked who humbled the people of God by their pride, when the children of God prayed, He intervened and shattered the wicked, as He drowned Pharaoh and all his army in the Red Sea, and killed 185,000 of the army of Sennacherib the Assyrian in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (Isa 37:36).

29.4.8.en: 3- The lofty cedar of Lebanon signifies the high places of the idol temples; God breaks them and brings His children back to faith in Him.

29.4.9.en: 4- God's power that breaks the cedars of Lebanon and casts them to the ground is like the calf of Lebanon that treads and crushes the grasses in the green, fertile regions spread across Lebanon. That is, the strongest thing on earth has no strength before God, and is like weak grass before the calf of Lebanon.

29.4.10.en: 5- The mountains too, however towering, cannot stand before the mighty voice of the Lord, but flee from His voice, as the young of the wild ox flee and run away. That is, everything great in creation cannot withstand the power of God, and this reassures the children of God that as long as God is with them, no one can harm them.

29.5.0.en: 7- "The voice of the Lord kindles flames of fire."

29.5.2.en: 1- God kindles the flame of fire by means of the lightning that appears in the sky and casts fire upon the earth.

29.5.3.en: 2- God punishes the wicked by kindling fire in their places, as He did in the seventh plague upon Pharaoh and the Egyptians, so that His people might go out of Egypt, when He sent fire along with the hail (Ex 9:24). And as He burned Sodom and Gomorrah with fire from heaven (Gen 19:24). And likewise He burned those who murmured against the priesthood of Aaron, with Korah, Dathan and Abiram (Num 16:35).

29.5.4.en: 3- God kindles by His Holy Spirit the fire of His love in the hearts of His children, so that they cling to Him, and He becomes their only aim, which rises above all aims, as we see in the lives of the martyrs, who sacrificed their lives for His name, and likewise the Apostles and servants who labored in His service, and in the hearts of those who left the world and lived solitary in monasticism to enjoy fellowship with Him, and the heart of every person who lives with God in His Church.

29.5.5.en: 4- In eternity God increases the kindling of love within the hearts of His children, so that they enjoy fellowship with Him forever, but for the wicked He kindles the flame of fire, which burns them and torments them forever.

29.5.6.en: 5- In the Septuagint, "God divides the flame of fire," and this actually happened with the three young men, when God divided the flame of fire and surrounded them with a covering of dewy air (Dan 3:50).

29.5.7.en: 6- God cuts off the flame of the fire of lusts and sin from the hearts of His children, and saves them from it, when they repent and return to Him.

29.6.0.en: 8- "The voice of the Lord shaketh the wilderness; the Lord shaketh the wilderness of Kadesh."

29.6.1.en: The wilderness of Kadesh: Kadesh means holy. The wilderness of Kadesh is the one the children of Israel crossed before entering the land of Canaan. It lies northeast of Sinai.

29.6.2.en: 1- In the wilderness of Kadesh, Moses spoke to the children of Israel in three long sermons, which are the Book of Deuteronomy. And after he sanctified them with the word of God, and shook their souls so that they would reject evil and enter the land of Canaan with pure hearts, he went up the mountain and died (Deut 34:5).

29.6.3.en: 2- The voice of the Lord is powerful in its speech, that is, it shakes the slack and lazy souls, so that they become alert in the wilderness of this world, and then they deserve to enter the land of Canaan, which signifies the Kingdom of Heaven.

29.6.4.en: 3- This quake also shakes the distant souls, like the Gentiles, so that they believe and have a place in the Kingdom of Heaven.

29.7.0.en: 9- "The voice of the Lord maketh the hinds to calve, and discovereth the forests: and in his temple every one saith, Glory."

29.7.1.en: The hind: the deer, or one of its kinds.

29.7.3.en: 1- Hinds give birth with difficulty and over a long time, but when they hear loud sounds they give birth quickly out of fear; so the voice of the Lord helps the believers to bring forth virtues, and to offer service and good works to those around them.

29.7.4.en: 2- The voice of the Lord is thunder and lightning, which, when it comes upon the forests, reveals what is inside them by the light of the lightning, shakes the trees and disturbs the animals, so that they come out of their dens and run far away.

29.7.5.en: So the voice of the Lord reveals man's sins, and every evil lust flees from it, and all anger, violence and savagery, and he is purified from all evil.

29.7.6.en: 3- After David reviewed the voice of the Lord that works in nature, whether the waters, or the cedars, or the flame of fire, or the wilderness, or the hinds, or the forests, he summarizes in conclusion and says that all nature, with the creatures of God in it, is worked upon by Him and is subject to Him; indeed, he declares that all of them are temples of God which He sanctified for Himself, and each of them glorifies God, as it says, "The heavens declare the glory of God" (Ps 19:1).

29.7.7.en: 4- Hinds search for serpents, and when they find them they trample them with their hooves and kill them, then eat them. So they purify the place of poisonous serpents, swallowing them and finishing them off. In this the power of God is shown, which overcomes evil and glorifies Him in His temple, which is the body of the hinds. For the hinds signify the spiritual person, who tramples Satan and his evil lusts, and triumphs over them, and so glorifies God in His temple, which is his body.

29.7.8.en: 5- If all nature is temples of God, then all the more the spiritual person is a temple of the Holy Spirit. And the Church is the greatest and holiest place in the world, because she is the temple of God in which all the believers raise their voices and glorify God with their praises and their works.

29.7.9.en: Your aim in life is to glorify God, by rejecting evil, walking uprightly and praising God, and this is an introduction to your eternal life. So remember your aim at the start of every day, so that you may live as a temple of the Holy Spirit.

29.8.s.en: (3) The sovereignty and blessing of the Lord

29.8.0.en: 10- "The Lord sitteth upon the flood; yea, the Lord sitteth King for ever."

29.8.1.en: 1- The voice of the Lord, repeated seven times, has done the following:

29.8.2.en: a - It thundered upon the waters and subjected them to Himself, and however great the power of the waves of the sea, He is the Controller of all, and so He reassures His children, however much wicked men rise up around them.

29.8.3.en: b - The voice of the Lord is with power, and it subdues the demons under the feet of His children.

29.8.4.en: c - The voice of the Lord appears with majesty, and gives His children awe in the eyes of those around them.

29.8.5.en: d - The voice of the Lord shatters the cedar, which is man's pride, and when he is crushed before God he receives His blessings.

29.8.6.en: e - The voice of the Lord kindles the fire of the Holy Spirit in the hearts of His children who believe in Him, so that they live with Him and keep His commandments.

29.8.7.en: f - It shakes the wilderness of our life, so that it is purified of all evil, that we may enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

29.8.8.en: g - The voice of the Lord makes the hind to calve and discovers the forests, so it purifies man of all evil, that he may live in purity before Him, filled with every virtue.

29.8.9.en: And in the end man becomes a true dwelling place for God and a temple for Him, and he glorifies Him.

29.8.10.en: 2- If the voice of God has prepared the souls of the believers and they have become a temple for Him, then He dwells in them, and sits, and rests in them through the sacrament of Baptism, which the flood signifies.

29.8.11.en: 3- The Lord sits upon the flood and puts an end to all evil, and delivers His children, who are Noah and his family, and also delivers His children in every generation, and sits in their hearts and never leaves them, and protects them from the works of Satan that surround them.

29.8.12.en: 4- God reigns over the hearts of His children and gives them the enjoyment of fellowship with Him, and He remains reigning over them forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

29.9.0.en: 11- "The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace."

29.9.1.en: 1- The Lord supports, lifts up and glorifies His children and His people, for He saves them from their sins and dwells in their hearts, so they lift up their heads rejoicing and praising God, who gives them victory every day over Satan.

29.9.2.en: 2- As God purifies His children every day by repentance, He grants them by His Holy Spirit good fruits, the most important of which is inner peace, which none but the children of God enjoy.

29.9.3.en: 3- If the voice of the Lord at the beginning of the psalm contains thunder, shattering, burning and quaking, all this is to purify His children from sin and remove from them all disturbance. Although it is a mighty voice, it is not frightening to the children of God; on the contrary, we find at the end of the psalm that He grants them His perfect peace.

29.9.4.en: The greatest grace that God gives you is inner peace, so cut off everything that hinders your peace and give it up, that you may enjoy the most precious jewel, which is peace, and then joy.

29.9.5.en: Thanksgiving to God the Savior. A Psalm and Song at the dedication of the house of David: "I will extol thee, O Lord; for thou hast lifted me up" (v. 1). Introduction:

29.9.6.en: 1- Its author: David the prophet, as appears from the title, and not Jeremiah, as some have claimed that he was its author, relying on what is written in the psalm, "Thou hast kept me alive, from among those that go down to the pit" (v. 3), because the intended meaning is symbolic, for God drew David up from death.

29.9.8.en: a - At the dedication of David's own house for his dwelling.

29.9.9.en: b - He said it in the field of Araunah the Jebusite, where he built an altar and gave thanks to God who stopped the plague. And there the temple of Solomon was built.

29.9.10.en: c - David said it when God forgave him his great sin with the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and that was by the hand of Nathan the prophet; so this sin is the severe sickness of which the psalm speaks to us, by which he drew near to death, and God healed him from it.

29.9.11.en: 3- This psalm was said at the dedication of the temple, whether in the days of Solomon, or Zerubbabel, or Judas Maccabeus, and it continued to be said at the Feast of Dedication until the days of Christ.

29.9.12.en: 4- Perhaps David wrote this psalm by the spirit of prophecy about King Hezekiah, who would be exposed to a sickness unto death, and after the prayer of Isaiah God healed him. And likewise about God's deliverance of Hezekiah from the army of Sennacherib, when the angel of God killed 185,000 soldiers of this army in one night.

29.9.13.en: 5- This psalm points to the birth of Christ and His resurrection by saying, "Thou hast brought up my soul from the grave, from among those that go down to the pit" (v. 3).

29.9.14.en: 6- In the title of this psalm we find "a Psalm and Song," and this means that it was said with two musical elements, or with one musical instrument, which is the pipe, that is, the "psalm," and the human voice, which is the "song."

29.9.15.en: 7- This psalm, with the four psalms that follow, that is, up to Psalm 34, are psalms of thanksgiving to God.

29.9.16.en: 8- The priest recites this psalm when he puts on the priestly vestments to begin the prayer of the Divine Liturgy.

29.9.17.en: 9- The Church recites this psalm in the prayer of the Third Hour, which is the hour of the descent of the Holy Spirit, because in this psalm appear the blessings of the work of the Holy Spirit in the life of the believer, so that he glorifies God.
